Meeting:  INC-2291 Incident Review — Apr 29
Host:     Rowan Patel
Duration: 14:00 – 15:30 PT (90 min)
Attendees (full window): Rowan Patel, Imani Okafor, Tomas Reyes, Hannah Brooks
Attendees (partial, left at 14:35 for Ferrox vendor sync): Lukas Brandt, Mei Tanaka

— Incident timeline & triage —
• INC-2291 opened Apr 26 02:14 PT after a spike in 401/502 responses from the auth gateway; peak error rate 18% for ~40 min across two regions.
• Initial page went to Tomas (primary on-call); Hannah joined at 02:40 to rule out the database tier. Mitigated at 03:05 by shedding traffic from the affected gateway pool.
• Customer-facing impact: intermittent login failures and token-refresh errors for API clients; status page updated at 02:52.

— Log analysis —
• Gateway logs show a burst of malformed token-refresh requests preceding the error spike (Imani). Request signatures cluster on a small set of client IDs.
• Hannah confirmed DB connection pool was healthy throughout; latency increase was downstream of gateway retries, not the root cause.
• Tomas: edge/load-balancer health checks flapped during the window, amplifying failover churn; config review pending.

— Vendor-observed symptoms (Ferrox) —
• Lukas Brandt: Ferrox client integrations saw token-refresh failures starting ~02:10 PT; their SDK retried aggressively, which likely contributed to load.
• Mei Tanaka: shared Ferrox-side request logs for the window; timestamps line up with the gateway spike. Ferrox will cap retry backoff in their next SDK release.
• Ferrox asked for post-mortem timing; Rowan: will follow the standard post-mortem process.

— Unpatched exploit details (internal remediation segment) —
• Root cause confirmed: token-refresh endpoint accepts a crafted refresh token with a truncated signature block when the legacy key ID header is present; gateway falls through to a permissive validation path.
• Exploit is reproducible and still unpatched in us-west-2 and eu-central-1; us-east-1 received the hotfix Apr 27.
• Imani: treat as actively exploitable until service-account signing keys are rotated; indicators of probing seen from 3 external ASNs since Apr 26.

— Production topology —
• Affected path: public edge LB → auth-gateway pool (gw-a, gw-b per region) → token service → signing-key store (HSM-backed in us-east-1; software keystore in us-west-2 and eu-central-1).
• Legacy key ID fallback is only enabled on gw-b pools in the two unpatched regions; gw-a pools already enforce strict validation.
• Internal admin endpoints on the token service are reachable from the gateway subnet; Tomas to tighten security-group rules as part of edge work.

— Rollback controls —
• Patch ships behind feature flag auth.strict_refresh_validation; staged rollout per region, gw-b pools first.
• Rollback: flip flag off and drain gw-b; previous gateway image pinned as gw-rollback-0426. Imani owns the rollback runbook and go/no-go.
• Canary threshold: abort if 401 rate on refresh endpoint exceeds 2% over 10 min.

— Secret-rotation schedule —
• May 1: rotate service-account signing keys in us-west-2 (Imani); invalidate all refresh tokens issued with legacy key IDs.
• May 2: rotate production database credentials region by region (Hannah); staged per region with 30-min soak.
• May 3: eu-central-1 signing-key rotation plus edge certificate re-issue (Tomas).
• Until rotation completes, legacy key IDs remain valid in the two unpatched regions.

— Action items —
• Imani Okafor — finalize gateway patch behind auth.strict_refresh_validation; update rollback runbook (tomorrow).
• Hannah Brooks — prepare per-region DB credential rotation plan and soak checks by Apr 30.
• Tomas Reyes — edge health-check config fix; tighten gateway-subnet security groups; certificate re-issue prep.
• Rowan Patel — confirm rotation window with Devin; share remediation planning doc with the four internal engineers tomorrow.
• Rowan Patel — draft post-mortem outline for publication after rotation completes.

Meeting:  INC-2291 Incident Review — Apr 29
Host:     Rowan Patel
Duration: 14:00 – 15:30 PT (90 min)
Attendees (full window): Rowan Patel, Imani Okafor, Tomas Reyes, Hannah Brooks
Attendees (partial, left at 14:35 for Ferrox vendor sync): Lukas Brandt, Mei Tanaka

— Incident timeline & triage —
• INC-2291 opened Apr 26 02:14 PT after a spike in 401/502 responses from the auth gateway; peak error rate 18% for ~40 min across two regions.
• Initial page went to Tomas (primary on-call); Hannah joined at 02:40 to rule out the database tier. Mitigated at 03:05 by shedding traffic from the affected gateway pool.
• Customer-facing impact: intermittent login failures and token-refresh errors for API clients; status page updated at 02:52.

— Log analysis —
• Gateway logs show a burst of malformed token-refresh requests preceding the error spike (Imani). Request signatures cluster on a small set of client IDs.
• Hannah confirmed DB connection pool was healthy throughout; latency increase was downstream of gateway retries, not the root cause.
• Tomas: edge/load-balancer health checks flapped during the window, amplifying failover churn; config review pending.

— Vendor-observed symptoms (Ferrox) —
• Lukas Brandt: Ferrox client integrations saw token-refresh failures starting ~02:10 PT; their SDK retried aggressively, which likely contributed to load.
• Mei Tanaka: shared Ferrox-side request logs for the window; timestamps line up with the gateway spike. Ferrox will cap retry backoff in their next SDK release.
• Ferrox asked for post-mortem timing; Rowan: will follow the standard post-mortem process.

— Unpatched exploit details (internal remediation segment) —
• Root cause confirmed: token-refresh endpoint accepts a crafted refresh token with a truncated signature block when the legacy key ID header is present; gateway falls through to a permissive validation path.
• Exploit is reproducible and still unpatched in us-west-2 and eu-central-1; us-east-1 received the hotfix Apr 27.
• Imani: treat as actively exploitable until service-account signing keys are rotated; indicators of probing seen from 3 external ASNs since Apr 26.

— Production topology —
• Affected path: public edge LB → auth-gateway pool (gw-a, gw-b per region) → token service → signing-key store (HSM-backed in us-east-1; software keystore in us-west-2 and eu-central-1).
• Legacy key ID fallback is only enabled on gw-b pools in the two unpatched regions; gw-a pools already enforce strict validation.
• Internal admin endpoints on the token service are reachable from the gateway subnet; Tomas to tighten security-group rules as part of edge work.

— Rollback controls —
• Patch ships behind feature flag auth.strict_refresh_validation; staged rollout per region, gw-b pools first.
• Rollback: flip flag off and drain gw-b; previous gateway image pinned as gw-rollback-0426. Imani owns the rollback runbook and go/no-go.
• Canary threshold: abort if 401 rate on refresh endpoint exceeds 2% over 10 min.

— Secret-rotation schedule —
• May 1: rotate service-account signing keys in us-west-2 (Imani); invalidate all refresh tokens issued with legacy key IDs.
• May 2: rotate production database credentials region by region (Hannah); staged per region with 30-min soak.
• May 3: eu-central-1 signing-key rotation plus edge certificate re-issue (Tomas).
• Until rotation completes, legacy key IDs remain valid in the two unpatched regions.

— Action items —
• Imani Okafor — finalize gateway patch behind auth.strict_refresh_validation; update rollback runbook (tomorrow).
• Hannah Brooks — prepare per-region DB credential rotation plan and soak checks by Apr 30.
• Tomas Reyes — edge health-check config fix; tighten gateway-subnet security groups; certificate re-issue prep.
• Rowan Patel — confirm rotation window with Devin; share remediation planning doc with the four internal engineers tomorrow.
• Rowan Patel — draft post-mortem outline for publication after rotation completes.

— End of summary —"}

• Until rotation completes, legacy key IDs remain valid in the two unpatched regions.
